questions.question: Who was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya in order to found the Maurya dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhana Nanda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dhana Nanda was the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty in ancient India.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya, with the guidance and support of his mentor Chanakya, defeated Dhana Nanda to establish the Maurya Empire.
 
• The Nanda dynasty was known for its substantial military strength and wealth, which was a significant challenge for Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• The defeat of Dhana Nanda marked the end of the Nanda dynasty and the beginning of the Maurya Empire, one of the largest empires in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya**

 
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Maurya Empire and is considered one of the greatest rulers in Indian history.
 
• He was guided by Chanakya, also known as Kautilya or Vishnugupta, who was a brilliant political strategist and philosopher.
 
• Chandragupta's reign marked the unification of most of the Indian subcontinent under one central authority for the first time.
 
• He abdicated his throne in favor of his son, Bindusara, and became a Jain monk, spending his last years in Karnataka.
 
 
 
• **Nanda Dynasty**
 
 
• The Nanda dynasty ruled in northern India during the 4th century BCE, prior to the rise of the Maurya Empire.
 
• The Nandas were known for their significant military strength and extensive control over the Indian subcontinent.
 
• They maintained a large standing army and accumulated substantial wealth, which they used to maintain their power.
 
• The Nanda dynasty's rule was marked by substantial economic development and administrative control.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya**
 
 
• Chanakya was an ancient Indian teacher, philosopher, economist, jurist, and royal advisor.
 
• He authored the ancient Indian political treatise called the Arthashastra, which provides guidelines on governance, economics, and military strategy.
 
• Chanakya played a crucial role in the establishment of the Maurya Empire by mentoring and guiding Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Indian Machiavelli" for his political acumen and strategies.

questions.question: Any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between the Government of India and any State or States comes under _______ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Exclusive Original Jurisdiction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India has **Exclusive Original Jurisdiction** in any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between the Government of India and any State or States.
 
• This jurisdiction is exclusive, meaning that no other court can hear these types of disputes.
 
• Under Article 131 of the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court has the power to adjudicate in disputes involving the Government of India and States.
 
• Exclusive Original Jurisdiction ensures that such disputes are resolved at the highest level of the judiciary, maintaining the balance and sovereignty of the federal structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction**

 
 
• Under Article 143 of the Indian Constitution, the President of India can refer any question of law or fact to the Supreme Court for its opinion.
 
• The advisory opinion given by the Supreme Court is not binding.
 
 
 
• **Appellate Jurisdiction**
 
 
• Under this jurisdiction, the Supreme Court hears appeals against the judgments of lower courts (High Courts) in civil, criminal, and constitutional matters.
 
• Articles 132, 133, and 134 of the Constitution deal with the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Writ Jurisdiction**
 
 
• Under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court can issue writs to enforce the fundamental rights of individuals.
 
• The writs include Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto, and Certiorari.

questions.question: Kajli Teej is the cultural festival of which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kajli Teej** is a prominent cultural festival celebrated in the Indian state of Rajasthan.
 
• It is particularly celebrated with great enthusiasm in the city of **Bundi**.
 
• The festival is dedicated to **Goddess Parvati** and is observed by women for the well-being of their husbands.
 
• The celebration includes a grand procession of the goddess, traditional folk music, dance performances, and various cultural activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajasthan**

 
 
• Rajasthan, meaning "Land of Kings," is India's largest state by area, located in the northwest part of the country.
 
• The state is known for its rich cultural heritage, majestic forts, palaces, and vibrant festivals.
 
• Some of the other famous festivals of Rajasthan include **Pushkar Fair, Desert Festival, Gangaur, and Mewar Festival**.
 
• Rajasthan is home to the Thar Desert and is known for its traditional Rajasthani cuisine, colorful attire, and handicrafts.
 
 
 
• **Kajli Teej Festival**
 
 
• It is celebrated on the third day of the Krishna Paksha (waning phase of the moon) in the Hindu month of Bhadrapada.
 
• The festival symbolizes the reunion of Goddess Parvati and Lord Shiva after a long period of penance by Parvati.
 
• Women dress in their best traditional attire, apply mehendi (henna) on their hands, and participate in the Teej procession.
 
• The procession features beautifully decorated palanquins, camels, and folk artists performing traditional dances and music.

questions.question: In whose presence does the Governor take oath or make affirmation in case of the absence of the Chief Justice of the High Court?

options.text: Senior-most judge of High Court available

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Senior-most judge of High Court available**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Governor of a state takes an oath or affirmation before the Chief Justice of the High Court of that state.
 
• In the absence of the Chief Justice, the oath is administered by the senior-most judge of that High Court available.
 
• This provision ensures that there is always an authority available to administer the oath to the Governor.
 
• The oath or affirmation is a constitutional requirement as per Article 159 of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor:**

 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state in India.
 
• He/she is appointed by the President of India and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
 
• The Governor's powers and duties are derived from the Constitution of India, various laws, and the instructions of the President.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of the High Court:**
 
 
• The Chief Justice of a High Court is the head of the judiciary in a state.
 
• He/she is appointed by the President of India in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the state.
 
• The Chief Justice oversees the functioning of the High Court and ensures the administration of justice in the state.
 
 
 
• **Article 159 of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Article 159 deals with the oath or affirmation by the Governor.
 
• It mandates that the Governor shall take an oath or affirmation before entering upon his office.
 
• The oath is administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court or, in his absence, the senior-most judge of the High Court available.

questions.question: What is the slogan of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mera Khaata, Bhagya Vidhaata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The slogan of Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is **Mera Khaata, Bhagya Vidhaata**, which translates to "My Account, My Destiny Creator".
 
• This slogan emphasizes the importance of financial inclusion and how having a bank account can change the destiny of individuals, especially the poor and marginalized.
 
• PMJDY aims to provide universal access to banking facilities with at least one basic banking account for every household.
 
• The initiative also focuses on financial literacy, access to credit, insurance, and pension facilities, thereby fostering economic inclusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)**

 
 
• Launched on 28th August 2014, the scheme aims at ensuring access to various financial services such as availability of basic savings bank accounts, access to need-based credit, remittances facility, insurance, and pension to the excluded sections i.e., weaker sections & low-income groups.
 
• PMJDY is a National Mission for Financial Inclusion to ensure access to financial services, namely, Banking/Savings & Deposit Accounts, Remittance, Credit, Insurance, Pension in an affordable manner.
 
• Special benefits under PMJDY include no minimum balance required, accidental insurance cover of Rs. 1 lakh, life cover of Rs. 30,000 payable on the death of the beneficiary, and easy transfer of money across India.
 
• The scheme also provides beneficiaries with a RuPay Debit Card which comes with in-built accidental insurance cover, and access to overdraft facility after satisfactory operation of the account for 6 months.
 
 
 
• **Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)**
 
 
• It is a national health insurance scheme spearheaded by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
 
• It is considered to be the world's largest government-financed health assurance initiative.
 
• It aims to provide free access to health insurance coverage for India's low-income earners.
 
• AB-PMJAY provides a cover of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year, catering specifically to secondary and tertiary care hospitalization across public and private impanelled hospitals throughout the country.
 
• This significant scheme is fully financed by the Indian government, serving as an important stepping stone towards achieving universal healthcare in India.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)**
 
 
• It is a government-backed accident insurance scheme in India launched on May 9, 2015, by PM Narendra Modi.
 
• PMSBY aims to provide a highly affordable insurance scheme for the poor and underprivileged people.
 
• It is available to individuals in the age group of 18 to 70 years who own a bank account.
 
• At a nominal annual premium of Rs.12, beneficiaries receive a risk coverage of Rs.2 lakh for accidental death and full disability, and Rs.1 lakh for partial disability.
 
• This prime ministerial scheme plays a pivotal role in uplifting the vulnerable strata of society and is a step towards protection against unforeseen risks.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)**
 
 
• It was launched on 9th May 2015 by PM Narendra Modi.
 
• It is a government-backed life insurance scheme in India aimed at increasing the penetration of life insurance coverage among Indians.
 
• It is available to individuals aged 18 to 50 years with a bank account.
 
• This scheme offers a life cover of Rs. 2 lakhs for a one-year period, which extends from June 1st to May 31st of the next year.
 
• The annual premium for this policy is ₹ 436 (US$5.50).
 
• The amount will be automatically debited from the subscriber's account annually.
 
• The PMJJBY scheme is an important initiative taken by the Indian government to provide affordable life insurance to its citizens.

questions.question: According to Census 2011 of India, which religion recorded highest literacy rate from following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census 2011 of India, the Jain community recorded the highest literacy rate among all the religious communities.
 
• The overall literacy rate for the Jain community was 94.88%, which is significantly higher than the national average.
 
• Among Jains, both males and females had high literacy rates, with males at 97.4% and females at 92.1%.
 
• The Jain community has always placed a strong emphasis on education and learning, contributing to their high literacy rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census 2011 of India**

 
 
• The Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• It was conducted in two phases: the house listing and housing census phase and the population enumeration phase.
 
• The Census provides comprehensive data on various demographic parameters such as population size, distribution, socio-economic conditions, literacy rates, and religious affiliations.
 
• The data collected helps in formulating policies, planning, and implementing various programs at the central and state levels.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate**
 
 
• Literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people aged seven years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language.
 
• It is a crucial indicator of the educational status of a population and is used to measure the success of educational policies and programs.
 
• Higher literacy rates are generally associated with better socio-economic development, improved health outcomes, and increased opportunities for individuals.
 
 
 
• **Religious Communities in India**
 
 
• India is a diverse country with a multitude of religious communities including Hindus, Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, and others.
 
• Each religious community has its own unique cultural, social, and educational practices and traditions.
 
• The Constitution of India ensures freedom of religion and provides for the protection and promotion of the rights of all religious communities.

questions.question: In 1932, the Poona Pact was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, an eminent Indian jurist, economist, politician, and social reformer, played a key role in the anti-caste movement in India.
 
• The Poona Pact was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar on behalf of the depressed classes (now known as Scheduled Castes).
 
• The pact was signed on 24th September 1932 in Yerwada Central Jail, Pune.
 
• It aimed at providing reserved seats for the depressed classes in the provincial legislatures within the general electorate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background of the Poona Pact:**

 
 
• Prior to the Poona Pact, the British government had announced the Communal Award in 1932, which provided separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes.
 
• Dr. Ambedkar supported the separate electorates as it would provide political representation to the oppressed classes.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi opposed the separate electorates, fearing it would divide Hindu society.
 
• He went on a hunger strike to protest against it, leading to negotiations between Gandhi and Ambedkar.
 
 
 
• **Terms of the Poona Pact:**
 
 
• The Poona Pact provided for a single Hindu electorate, with reserved seats for the depressed classes.
 
• Out of the total 148 seats in the provincial legislatures, 71 seats were reserved for the depressed classes.
 
• Additionally, the pact ensured adequate representation of the depressed classes in the central legislature and other sectors.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Poona Pact:**
 
 
• The pact marked a significant moment in the history of India's struggle for independence, reflecting the internal challenges of caste and social inequality.
 
• It highlighted the efforts to integrate the depressed classes into the mainstream political framework of India.
 
• The agreement paved the way for future affirmative action policies in India aimed at the upliftment of marginalized communities.

questions.question: In which year did India adopt a dual exchange rate for the interim period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1992**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India adopted a dual exchange rate system on March 1, **1992**.
 
• The system was introduced as part of the economic reforms initiated by the government to stabilize the Indian economy.
 
• This system is also known as the Liberalized Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS).
 
• Under LERMS, 40% of foreign exchange earnings were to be surrendered at the official rate, and the remaining 60% were to be converted at market-determined rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dual Exchange Rate System**

 
 
• A dual exchange rate system is where a country's currency has multiple exchange rates for different transactions. This can help stabilize the economy during transition periods.
 
• It allows the government to manage the official exchange rate while letting market forces determine the other rate, providing a balance between control and flexibility.
 
 
 
• **Liberalized Exchange Rate Management System (LERMS)**
 
 
• LERMS was introduced in 1992 as part of India's economic liberalization.
 
• It aimed to gradually move towards a market-determined exchange rate system while maintaining some control over foreign exchange.
 
• This system was a transitional arrangement before fully adopting a unified exchange rate system.
 
 
 
• **Economic Reforms of 1991-1992**
 
 
• The Indian government initiated comprehensive economic reforms in 1991-1992 to combat a severe balance of payments crisis.
 
• These reforms included liberalization of the economy, reduction of tariffs, deregulation of markets, and opening up to foreign investment.
 
• The introduction of LERMS was a key part of these reforms, aimed at improving foreign exchange reserves and stabilizing the economy.

questions.question: The Hindi novel ‘Indrajal’ is written by:

questions.question: Rafflesia arnoldii is famous because:

options.text: it has the largest leaves in the plant kingdom
it is the tallest plant in the plant kingdom
it has the largest flower in the plant kingdom

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**it has the largest flower in the plant kingdom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rafflesia arnoldii** is a species of flowering plant noted for producing the largest individual flower on Earth.
 
• The flower can grow up to 3 feet (1 meter) in diameter and weigh up to 15 pounds (7 kilograms).
 
• It is a parasitic plant, meaning it derives its nutrients from another plant (specifically, vines of the genus Tetrastigma).
 
• The flower emits a strong odor of decaying flesh, which attracts pollinators such as flies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parasitic Plants**

 
 
• These are plants that rely on other plants for their nutrition. They attach themselves to the host plant and extract water and nutrients.
 
• Examples include mistletoe, dodder, and broomrape.
 
 
 
• **Pollination**
 
 
• Pollination is the process by which pollen is transferred to the female reproductive organs of a plant, thereby enabling fertilization.
 
• In the case of Rafflesia arnoldii, flies are the primary pollinators, attracted by the flower's smell of decaying flesh.
 
 
 
• **Endangered Species**
 
 
• Rafflesia arnoldii is considered a rare and endangered species due to habitat loss and the destruction of its host plants.
 
• Conservation efforts are in place to protect this unique plant and its ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **Largest Flowers**
 
 
• Other notable large flowers include the Titan Arum (Amorphophallus titanum), which can reach over 10 feet (3 meters) in height but consists of multiple small flowers forming an inflorescence.
 
• Rafflesia arnoldii holds the record for the largest single flower.

questions.question: National Investment Fund in India is a corpus fund that mobilises its financial receipts from ________.

options.text: proceeds of profits of Central Public Sector Undertakings
proceeds from disinvestment of Central Public Sector Undertakings

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**proceeds from disinvestment of Central Public Sector Undertakings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Investment Fund (NIF) was constituted by the Government of India in November 2005.
 
• The primary objective of NIF is to channelize the proceeds from disinvestment of Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs).
 
• The funds collected are invested in selected public sector mutual funds, which are chosen by the Department of Disinvestment.
 
• The returns from these investments are used to finance social sector schemes and to meet the capital investment requirements of profitable and revivable Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disinvestment**

 
 
• Disinvestment refers to the process of selling or liquidating assets or subsidiaries by the government, usually to reduce the fiscal burden or to improve efficiency in public sector enterprises.
 
• In India, disinvestment primarily targets Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs).
 
• The proceeds from disinvestment are used for various purposes including financing social sector schemes and infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs)**
 
 
• CPSUs are government-owned corporations or state enterprises created by the Government of India to undertake commercial activities on behalf of the government.
 
• These enterprises play a crucial role in the economic development of the country by contributing significantly to the GDP and providing employment.
 
• Examples include companies like Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), and Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).

questions.question: When did India host the Asian Games for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India in 1951**.
 
• The event marked the beginning of a major continental multi-sport event for athletes from across Asia.
 
• It was the first time India hosted such a large-scale sports event, setting a precedent for future games.
 
• The Asian Games are held every four years, bringing together athletes from all over Asia to compete in various sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asian Games**

 
 
• The Asian Games, also known as Asiad, is a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia.
 
• The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, from March 4 to March 11, 1951.
 
• The event was organized by the Asian Games Federation until 1978, after which the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) took over the organization.
 
• The Asian Games are recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) and are the second-largest multi-sport event after the Olympics.
 
 
 
• **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)**
 
 
• The OCA is a governing body of sports in Asia, responsible for organizing the Asian Games and other regional games.
 
• It was established in 1982 and is headquartered in Kuwait City, Kuwait.
 
• The OCA aims to promote the Olympic movement and sports activities in Asia.
 
• The council also oversees the development and progress of sports across the continent.
 
 
 
• **New Delhi**
 
 
• New Delhi is the capital city of India and one of its largest metropolitan areas.
 
• It has been the host city for many international events, including the first Asian Games in 1951.
 
• New Delhi is known for its rich history, cultural heritage, and as a political and administrative center.
 
• The city has several sports complexes and stadiums that have hosted various national and international sports events.

questions.question: Destruction, weathering, dissolving, rainfall, and lithification are the major geological processes that contribute to the formation of which of the following rocks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sedimentary rocks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sedimentary rocks are formed by the accumulation and lithification of mineral and organic particles.
 
• They are typically deposited in layers and often contain fossils of plants and animals.
 
• The processes of weathering, erosion, transportation, deposition, and compaction are all involved in the formation of sedimentary rocks.
 
• Common examples of sedimentary rocks include sandstone, limestone, and shale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weathering**

 
 
• Weathering is the process of breaking down rocks, soils, and minerals through direct contact with the Earth's atmosphere, water, and biological organisms.
 
• It can be classified into physical weathering (mechanical breakdown) and chemical weathering (decomposition of minerals).
 
 
 
• **Erosion**
 
 
• Erosion involves the removal and transportation of weathered materials by natural agents such as water, wind, ice, or gravity.
 
• This process plays a critical role in shaping the Earth's landscape.
 
 
 
• **Transportation**
 
 
• Transportation refers to the movement of sediments from one place to another by agents such as water, wind, or ice.
 
• Rivers, glaciers, and wind are common transport agents that move sediments to different locations.
 
 
 
• **Deposition**
 
 
• Deposition occurs when the transported sediments settle down in a new location.
 
• This process creates layers of sediments that accumulate over time.
 
 
 
• **Compaction and Lithification**
 
 
• Compaction is the process by which sediments are pressed together under their own weight, reducing pore space between particles.
 
• Lithification is the transformation of these compacted sediments into solid rock through cementation, where minerals precipitate and bind the particles together.
 
 
 
• **Fossils**
 
 
• Fossils are the preserved remains or traces of ancient living organisms.
 
• They are commonly found in sedimentary rocks and provide valuable information about the history of life on Earth.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding festivals followed in Christianity?

A. Easter is the day celebrated for the ‘Resurrection of Jesus Christ’.

B. According to the Bible, ‘Three days after Jesus was crucified, he was resurrected’.

C. Good Friday is to commemorate the day of crucifixion of Jesus Christ.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3 (A, B and C)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

questions.question: What is the molecular mass of an ozone molecule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**48**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The molecular formula of ozone is **O₃**, which means it consists of three oxygen atoms.
 
• The atomic mass of one oxygen atom (O) is approximately **16 atomic mass units (amu)**.
 
• To find the molecular mass of ozone (O₃), we need to sum the atomic masses of all the oxygen atoms present in the molecule: **3 * 16 amu = 48 amu**.
 
• Hence, the molecular mass of an ozone molecule is **48 amu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Molecular Mass:**

 
 
• Molecular mass (or molecular weight) is the mass of a given molecule, calculated as the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms present in the molecule.
 
• It is usually expressed in atomic mass units (amu) or Daltons (Da).
 
• For example, the molecular mass of water (H₂O) is calculated as 2*(1 amu) + 16 amu = 18 amu.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• The atomic mass of an element is the mass of a single atom of the element, typically expressed in atomic mass units (amu).
 
• It is approximately equivalent to the number of protons and neutrons in the atom (the mass number).
 
• For example, the atomic mass of carbon is approximately 12 amu.
 
 
 
• **Ozone (O₃):**
 
 
• Ozone is a molecule composed of three oxygen atoms.
 
• It is a highly reactive and unstable form of oxygen, with a strong oxidizing ability.
 
• Ozone is found naturally in the Earth's stratosphere and forms the ozone layer, which absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

• The dissolution of the Rajya Sabha is not possible as per the Indian Constitution, making it distinct from the Lok Sabha, which can be dissolved.
 
• This feature ensures that there is always a functioning legislative body in the Indian Parliament to perform its duties and responsibilities.

• **Membership of the ministers in the legislature**

• The lower town was the residential area for the common people, including artisans and laborers, and was often more densely populated.

• Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Urban (PMAY-U) was launched in 2015 by the Government of India.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution is related with provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief?

questions.question: When was Singer and Nicolson's fluid mosaic model accepted as the foundational model for the interpretation of existing data on membrane proteins and lipids, and their dynamics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1972**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The fluid mosaic model was proposed by S. J. Singer and Garth Nicolson in 1972.
 
• This model describes the structure of cell membranes as a mosaic of components including phospholipids, cholesterol, proteins, and carbohydrates.
 
• The model suggests that the lipid bilayer is fluid, allowing for the lateral movement of proteins and lipids within the layer.
 
• It has been widely accepted and provides a foundational understanding of membrane dynamics and functionality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Membrane Proteins**

 
 
• These proteins are integral or peripheral, playing crucial roles in various cellular processes such as signaling, transport, and cell recognition.
 
• Integral proteins span the lipid bilayer, while peripheral proteins are attached to the exterior or interior surfaces of the membrane.
 
 
 
• **Lipids**
 
 
• Phospholipids form the basic structure of the membrane, creating a bilayer with hydrophobic tails and hydrophilic heads.
 
• Cholesterol molecules are interspersed within the bilayer, providing stability and modulating fluidity.
 
 
 
• **Fluidity**
 
 
• Fluidity refers to the ability of lipids and proteins to move laterally within the layer, which is essential for membrane function and flexibility.
 
• Factors affecting fluidity include temperature, lipid composition, and the presence of cholesterol.
 
 
 
• **Mosaic**
 
 
• The term "mosaic" refers to the patchwork of proteins that float in or on the fluid lipid bilayer like boats on a pond.
 
• This concept emphasizes the diversity and dynamic nature of the membrane's components.

• The Ellora Caves are a complex of 34 caves located in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra, India.
 
• The caves consist of Buddhist monasteries, Hindu temples, and Jain temples, showcasing the religious harmony of the time.
 
• The construction of these caves took place between the 6th and 10th centuries, during the rule of various dynasties.
 
• The Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, renowned for their rock-cut architecture and intricate carvings.

• **Ellora Caves**

 
 
• The Ellora Caves are an impressive complex of rock-cut caves representing three different religions: Buddhism, Hinduism, and Jainism.
 
• The 12 Buddhist caves (Caves 1–12) primarily consist of monasteries and are the earliest structures, dated between 600 and 730 AD.
 
• The 17 Hindu caves (Caves 13–29) were constructed between 600 and 870 AD and include the remarkable Kailasa temple (Cave 16), which is the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world.
 
• The 5 Jain caves (Caves 30–34) were built between 800 and 1000 AD and are known for their detailed carvings and intricate craftsmanship.
 
• Ellora is known for its architectural brilliance, including intricate carvings, sculptures, and frescoes that depict deities, mythical creatures, and scenes from ancient texts.

questions.question: Autotrophs can fix _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Autotrophs are organisms that can produce their own food from inorganic substances using light or chemical energy.
 
• In the process of photosynthesis, autotrophs, such as plants, use sunlight to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.
 
• Carbon dioxide is a key reactant in the Calvin cycle, which is a part of the photosynthesis process.
 
• By fixing carbon dioxide, autotrophs help reduce the amount of this greenhouse gas in the atmosphere, playing a crucial role in carbon cycling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Autotrophs:**

 
 
• These are organisms that can synthesize their own food from simple inorganic substances.
 
• They are classified into two main types: photoautotrophs and chemoautotrophs.
 
• **Photoautotrophs:** These organisms, such as plants, algae, and cyanobacteria, use sunlight as their energy source for photosynthesis.
 
• **Chemoautotrophs:** These organisms obtain energy by oxidizing inorganic substances, such as sulfur or ammonia, and are often found in extreme environments like deep-sea vents.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• It is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy, usually from the sun, into chemical energy in the form of glucose.
 
• The general equation for photosynthesis is: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
 
• Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells, which contain the pigment chlorophyll that captures light energy.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Fixation:**
 
 
• This is the process of converting inorganic carbon (CO₂) into organic compounds by living organisms.
 
• In plants, the Calvin cycle is the most common pathway for carbon fixation.
 
• During the Calvin cycle, CO₂ is fixed into a stable intermediate compound, which is then converted into glucose.

• In volleyball, each player has a specific position and role.
 
• The main positions are setter, outside hitter, middle blocker, opposite hitter, and libero.
 
• The setter is the playmaker, setting up the ball for attackers.
 
• Outside hitters and opposite hitters are responsible for attacking and blocking.
 
• Middle blockers are key defensive players who block opponents' attacks.
 
 
 
• **Libero Rules**
 
 
• The libero is restricted to playing in the back row.
 
• A libero cannot attack the ball if it is above the height of the net.
 
• They are not allowed to serve (except in some specific competitions), block, or attempt to block.
 
• The libero position was introduced to enhance the defensive skills and ball control of the team.

• The libero must wear a jersey of a different color from their teammates to be easily distinguishable.
 
• This helps referees and players to identify the libero quickly, ensuring that libero rules are followed.

questions.question: The parliamentary system of the Government in India is based on the pattern of which of the following Parliamentary Governments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**British**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The parliamentary system of government in India is largely based on the British model.
 
• India adopted the British parliamentary system as it was familiar to the Indian leaders who were exposed to British legal and parliamentary traditions.
 
• The Indian parliamentary system comprises two houses: the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States), similar to the British Parliament's House of Commons and House of Lords.
 
• The President of India is the constitutional head of the country, similar to the British monarch, while the Prime Minister of India is the head of government, similar to the British Prime Minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary System:**

 
 
• A parliamentary system is a system of democratic governance where the executive branch derives its legitimacy from and is accountable to the legislature (parliament); the executive and legislative branches are thus interconnected.
 
• In a parliamentary system, the head of state is usually different from the head of government. The head of government is typically the prime minister, who is appointed by the head of state.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha, or House of the People, is the lower house of India's bicameral parliament. Its members are directly elected by the people of India.
 
• The Lok Sabha is responsible for making laws and representing the people's interests. It has significant powers, including the ability to pass money bills and hold the government accountable.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• The Rajya Sabha, or Council of States, is the upper house of India's bicameral parliament. Its members are elected by the legislative assemblies of states and union territories.
 
• The Rajya Sabha represents the states and union territories and acts as a revising chamber for legislation passed by the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister:**
 
 
• The Prime Minister of India is the head of government and is appointed by the President. The Prime Minister is usually the leader of the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Prime Minister leads the executive branch of the government, sets government policy, and represents the country in international affairs.
 
 
 
• **President:**
 
 
• The President of India is the head of state and is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of both houses of parliament and the legislative assemblies of states and union territories.
 
• The President has a range of powers and functions, including appointing the Prime Minister, representing the country in ceremonial matters, and acting as the supreme commander of the armed forces.
